method: Conservative manually-audited probability layer. Polling margin is shrunk toward historical partisan baseline and converted with a 4–7 point race-error scale; chamber control uses generic-ballot and seat-map uncertainty. Probabilities are rounded to avoid false precision.

Will the Democratic Party win the U.S. H.reason: A roughly D+8 national environment makes a Democratic House majority the modal outcome, with meaningful district-map uncertainty.

Will the Republican Party win the U.S. S.reason: Republicans retain a narrow structural advantage, but an expanded battleground under a Democratic national environment keeps control close.
assumptions: Seat outcomes correlated through national swing
Candidate polling weighted more than presidential baseline

Will the Democratic Party win the Texas.reason: Texas is unusually competitive, but its Republican statewide baseline still narrowly outweighs the Democratic national environment.
assumptions: Texas baseline remains several points right of nation

Will the Democratic Party win the North.reason: The Democratic national edge moves a historically close state slightly Democratic, but the race remains error-sensitive.

Will the Democratic Party win the Maine.reason: Maine leans Democratic federally, but incumbency and state-specific ticket splitting keep the outcome uncertain.

Will the Republican Party win the Georgi.reason: Georgia is a true battleground; the national environment gives Democrats a modest advantage rather than a safe lead.
assumptions: No runoff-specific discount unless required by market rules

Will the Republican Party win the Arizon.reason: Available polling showed a sizable Democratic advantage; staleness is reflected in only medium confidence.
assumptions: Older polling receives strong uncertainty inflation

Will the Democratic Party win the NY-17.reason: A Republican-held Biden-friendly district becomes Democratic-leaning in a strong national Democratic environment.
assumptions: Generic-ballot swing partially transfers to district
Incumbency offsets part of national swing

Will the Democratic Party win the PA-07.reason: The district is highly competitive; the Democratic national lead creates only a modest advantage after local uncertainty.

Will the Democratic Party win the New Ha.reason: The latest cited state average put the Democrat about six points ahead in a Democratic national environment.

Will the Republican Party win the New Ha.reason: Complement of the modeled Democratic New Hampshire Senate probability.
assumptions: Binary party outcome under resolution rules

Will the Democratic Party win the Massac.reason: A large Democratic polling and historical partisan advantage makes an upset remote.

Will the Republican Party win the Massac.reason: Complement of the strongly Democratic Massachusetts Senate estimate.
assumptions: Binary party outcome under resolution rules

Will the Democratic Party win the Oklaho.reason: Oklahoma's long-run Republican federal baseline overwhelms the national Democratic swing.

Will the Democratic Party win the Alaska.reason: Current polling aggregation showed the Democrat narrowly ahead, but Alaska's system and small electorate widen uncertainty.
assumptions: Ranked-choice dynamics included only through wider uncertainty

Will the Republican Party win the Alaska.reason: Complement of the modeled Democratic Alaska Senate probability.
assumptions: Binary party outcome under resolution rules

Will the Democratic Party win the Rhode.reason: Rhode Island's historical federal baseline makes a Republican Senate upset remote.

Will the Republican Party win the Rhode.reason: Complement of the strongly Democratic Rhode Island Senate estimate.
assumptions: Binary party outcome under resolution rules

Will the Democratic Party win the Rhode.reason: The state's Democratic baseline makes the Democrat a strong favorite, with more gubernatorial ticket-splitting uncertainty than in federal races.

Will the Republican Party win the Rhode.reason: Complement of the modeled Democratic Rhode Island gubernatorial probability.
assumptions: Binary party outcome under resolution rules
